source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: 【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). 【During Test】 Hardware required: RDIMM with ECC / HDT Software tool: AMD RAS Error Injection Tool 1. BIOS settings: a. CPU Common Options → Platform First Error Handling: Enabled b. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh enable: TRUE c. CPU Common Options → MCA error thresh count: FFE (Deviate from default setting FF5) d. CPU Common Options → SMU and PSP Debug Mode: Disabled e. FCH Common Options → FCH RAS Options → Reset After Sync-Flood: Enable 2. Unlock CPU via HDT. 3. Boot into Ubuntu 20.04/RHEL 9.0 / Windows 2022. 4. Download the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool, then install and open the software. 5. Correctable Error Injection sudo ./cmdline_amdraserrorinjectiontest --smupsp --socket 0 --errormode 2 --ccd 0 --enablemcapolling 0 --errorindex 0 --errortype 0 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: PARTIAL | -- MP5 Correctable Error: inject the MP5 MP5 Correctable Error via the AMD RAS Error Injection Tool (after HDT/unlock + the BIOS RAS knobs from the procedure, e.g. Platform First Error Handling=Enabled + per-unit MCA/UMC settings). Agent stages/verifies with sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "dmesg -T 2>&1 | tail -160 | grep -iE 'smu|mp1|mp5|mpio|firmware.error|corrected|uncorrected'; echo __MP5_MP5_Correctable_Error; ipmitool sel elist 2>&1 | tail -40 2>&1" but the tool injection step itself is interactive/HW-level and needs the user to drive the exact inject command.

test_case.test_name: MP5 Correctable Error — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Inject one correctable MP5 error at the intended CCD and firmware index, verify a fresh MP5-specific corrected event without reset or escalation, then prove CCD compute and MP5-managed services remain healthy.
required_package: MP5 controller-to-socket/CCD/core/NUMA map and required coverage
Vendor semantics for errormode2, CCD0, enablemcapolling0, errorindex0 and errortype0
FFE threshold and SMU/PSP-debug-disable relevance with raw restoration values
Exact MP5 CE source/severity/count and no-reset/no-UCE acceptance
Supported OS and timeout plus CCD compute, NUMA, sensor and firmware-service limits
Abort, recovery, cleanup and BIOS/HDT restoration
test_case.test_command: Map MP5, socket and CCD instances; validate errormode2/index0/mcapolling0/errortype0; preserve raw state/log baseline; inject once; correlate exactly one fresh MP5 CE; check no reset/UCE and verify CCD cores, NUMA, sensors and workload health; restore all temporary RAS/HDT settings.
test_case.expected_result: 1. For correctable errors, the tool provides a PASS status. 2. For uncorrectable errors, verify that the errors are logged correctly in BERT dmesg after the warm reset is triggered. 3. If the OS reports the error within a timeout period, the test passed. 4. If the OS does not report the error within a timeout period, the test failed.
